summary: Validated the new to-call entry rule (OR with call_attempts) and the Injoignable 6-call gate interaction. Created /app/backend/tests/test_to_call_entry_rule.py with 9 focused tests covering all scenarios requested by the main agent. All 9/9 pass.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2759 lines — well above the 700-line guideline; should be split into modules (routers/, services/) in a future refactor.

The to-call main loop (lines 1592-1676) and older-open-count loop (1700-1708) both duplicate the is_tracked-or-call_attempts gating logic. Consider extracting a helper `_is_in_tracked_pipeline(doc) -> bool` to prevent future drift between the two endpoints.
seed_data_creation: Each test creates its own test lead via POST /api/admin/notifications/test-lead (store=test, is_test=true) and deletes it in a finally block. No persistent test data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The new to-call entry rule is: `if not created_at or not (is_tracked or call_attempts): continue` — mirrored in both GET /admin/to-call and GET /admin/to-call/older-open-count. _unreachable_rule_satisfied bypasses the 6-call rule ONLY when not is_tracked AND zero call_attempts. All 9 scenarios from the review request are now covered by test_to_call_entry_rule.py (old lead excluded from to-call, counted in older-open, decremented after 1 call, group 3 after backdated call, callback group 1 flow, injoignable bypass with 0 calls, injoignable blocked after 1 call, injoignable allowed after 6 pas_de_reponse, regression check tracked lead=group 2).
rca of the issue: N/A — this iteration validates a backend rule fix the main agent already deployed. No bugs found.
